lens: Generative UI: the AI composes the debrief and coaching layout per call (AI SDK generative UI)
name: Composed Coaching Console
one_liner: A fixed design system in which the AI composes each call's live coaching and debrief from a closed set of typed blocks, so every layout is personal to the call yet unmistakably on-brand.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed: the debrief is composed per call. The grader streams an ordered plan of typed blocks (ScoreHero, MomentReplay, CriterionCard, PatternCallout, DrillCTA), and the coach streams cue blocks during the call. Changed: research showed the AI SDK's streamUI (React Server Components) is marked experimental, so I use AI SDK UI (useChat plus typed tool parts) with a client-side block registry. The model picks blocks and their order from a closed catalogue and never emits markup, which protects brand, accessibility and reliability. Every block must cite transcript turn IDs that validate against the transcript, with a classic fixed-order debrief as fallback. Self-scores (1-10): A 8, B 7, C 8, D 6 (only if cue latency stays under about 1.5 s), E 6, F1 6, F2 5, F3 3 (leans worth building).

design_language.typography: Geist Sans: 600 for display, 400 for body at 16/24 minimum. Geist Mono for timers, scores and timestamps. Debrief grade numeral set at 56/60 in Mono.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radius 14px cards, 10px controls, 999px chips. Depth from hairlines and tonal surface steps. Live elements get a 1px signal glow ring. No blurred gradient orb.
design_language.motion: Blocks stream in with a 180ms rise and fade. Meters tween over 600ms. Cue cards enter from the rail edge and dismiss after 8s unless pinned. Everything reduces to opacity under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 16 and 20px, stroke 1.75. AI-generated content carries a single spark glyph in signal colour so the rep always knows what the model wrote.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark default for the live console and focus; light for the library, progress and print-friendly debrief. Both via :root tokens with data-theme, following prefers-color-scheme when unset.

navigation_and_ia: Top bar: Practice, Library, Progress, Team (org accounts only), a Cmd/Ctrl+K palette to start any persona, and a primary Build persona button. Routes: /, /library, /library/[slug], /wizard, /practice/[scenario], /call/[id], /debrief/[id], /progress, /team. Mobile uses a bottom tab bar: Practice, Library, Progress, Me. Coach mode (Blind, Guided, Coached) is visible before, during and after every call, not buried in settings.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Two streams. The coach runs a small OpenAI-compatible model on each rep turn, debounced, and streams typed cue blocks (whisper, objection alert, next question, talk-track step) plus rubric deltas. Each cue cites the transcript turn it reacts to, and the persona never sees coaching. Coach mode fades scaffolding: Blind shows only the score after the call, Guided adds cues and live meters, Coached adds interrupt-style nudges. Live scores are labelled as estimates. The final grade still comes from the full rubric grader with verbatim quotes. Cap at three cues per minute so the rail never overwhelms the rep, and show a small cost meter for the session.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library ships as data packs: one JSON or YAML file per persona holding role, seniority, temperament, objections, opening line, voice ID and rubric weights, validated by zod in CI. Target at launch: about 150 personas across the 18 industries in the brief and six job families (SDR cold, AE discovery, CS, support, collections, recruiting). The wizard turns a job description, product URL, CRM note or pasted call into a draft pack, with provenance chips on every field and a rehearsal before save. Its export is the same pack file, so the wizard doubles as a contributor on-ramp for the open-source core.
signature_moments: The debrief opens on the one moment that cost the deal, not on a letter grade.
A whisper cue appears in amber, quotes the exact line that triggered it, then fades.
The live rubric strip ticks up in real time as the rep covers each criterion.
Every AI-composed block carries a why chip that links to validated transcript turns.
A three-position Coach mode dial (Blind, Guided, Coached) that makes scaffolding visible.
The persona wizard streams a persona card field by field, each field with a source chip.
openai_fund_angle: Show the models in the UI: a model-slot strip on the landing page, and in every debrief footer the grader model name, rubric version and token cost, so reviewers see efficient use of API credits. Offer the OpenAI Realtime API as a voice path beside the ElevenLabs default. Invite contributors by design: persona packs and blocks are plain files with an Add a persona with Codex guide, and the wizard exports a PR-ready pack. Use Codex in pull-request review and release notes, and say so in the README, so the project visibly meets the program's PR-review and maintainer-automation criteria. Program scope from the sources: the Codex Open Source Fund grants up to $25,000 in API credits for projects using Codex CLI and OpenAI models, and Codex for Open Source adds a ChatGPT Pro benefit with Codex access and conditional Codex Security for selected maintainers.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (weeks 1-2): Tailwind v4 and shadcn/ui init, token migration, Geist in place of Inter and Sora, rebuilt AppShell, buttons and cards. Phase 2: live call console and block registry behind a feature flag, with the current debrief kept as fallback. Phase 3: debrief composer, then the persona pack loader and library. Phase 4: wizard, landing hero, progress and team views. Scenarios move from localStorage to pack files, with Prisma for org overrides. Existing API routes and the grader contract stay unchanged.

risks: AI-composed layouts can drift or read as inconsistent; mitigate with a closed block registry, a layout grammar and the classic fixed-order fallback.
Live coach latency and token cost; mitigate with a small model, debounced turns, a cue cap and a visible cost meter.
Live scores can look authoritative; label them as estimates and keep the final rubric grade canonical.
Persona quality depends on authoring; mitigate with pack CI, schema validation and a review checklist for contributors.
Copy-in shadcn code adds maintenance; document ownership and pin versions.
Streaming cues can overload screen-reader users; use aria-live polite with throttling and a text transcript path.
Second Nature, Hyperbound and Yoodli already market live coaching; our edge is open, inspectable and forkable, and the team needs to prove it in the demo.
